items.q: he worked with us, with Roy, in the Three Deuces for awhile.

ctx.x: Was there any kind of regional music that they grew out of?

I just can't -- I don't know what to attribute it to, you know, just a feeling that was just there, you know. And Chicago kind of had its own thing too. But out of this midwest you had Lester, Budd, Buster Smith, Dick Wilson. These are all tremendous reed men. And they had some very good swing drummers, just pure swing. It was just a pleasure. One of the gentlemen came from Kansas City and played with us awhile, by the name of Jesse Price. Ok sure. (Inaudible).

Yeah, well Jesse was quite a drummer, in his time, and he worked with us, with Roy, in the Three Deuces for awhile. Very good drummer. We used to call him Bopbop. But the midwest had its own thing, you know, so they would come from Kansas City to Chicago and from there, and Jesse Stone also. I don't know whether I mentioned Jesse Stone.
